skill.description: Generate text-to-video videos with HappyHorse 1.0 through the RunComfy CLI, including prompt guidance, input schema, and model selection advice.
skill.summary: Create HappyHorse 1.0 text-to-video outputs through RunComfy with structured prompts and CLI examples.
skill.author: agentspace-so

security_audit.summary: The skill primarily documents a legitimate RunComfy text-to-video workflow, including expected CLI commands and outbound RunComfy API access. Most static hits are Markdown backticks, code fences, URL documentation, or ellipses in API paths rather than malicious behavior. The remaining confirmed issues are the intended external CLI and third-party network dependency, so users should install and run it only when they trust RunComfy and understand credential handling.

remediation.issue: External CLI execution is central to the skill.
remediation.suggestion: Tell users to review the RunComfy CLI package before installation and run commands only in trusted environments.

remediation.issue: Prompts and job metadata are sent to a third-party API.
remediation.suggestion: Warn users not to include secrets, private customer data, or unreleased content in prompts unless their RunComfy account and policies permit it.

remediation.issue: Credential storage depends on the local RunComfy CLI.
remediation.suggestion: Recommend RUNCOMFY_TOKEN for CI and confirm local token files use owner-only permissions.

content.value_statement: Video creators need reliable prompts and settings for high quality text-to-video generation. This skill guides Claude, Codex, or Claude Code through HappyHorse 1.0 requests using the RunComfy CLI.
actual_capabilities: Explains when to choose HappyHorse 1.0 instead of nearby RunComfy video models.
Documents supported text-to-video fields such as prompt, aspect ratio, resolution, duration, seed, and watermark.
Provides RunComfy CLI commands for default, vertical, and lower cost test generations.
Gives prompt writing guidance for motion, camera direction, multi-shot consistency, and audio direction.
Summarizes CLI exit codes, polling behavior, token handling, and output download behavior.
limitations: Requires an installed RunComfy CLI and a valid RunComfy account or token.
Covers the text-to-video endpoint only, not a separate image-to-video pipeline.
Generated clips are limited to the model duration and aspect ratio options documented by RunComfy.
Prompts and generated outputs are sent to a third-party RunComfy service.

use_cases.title: Prototype a brand video
use_cases.description: Create a short 1080p concept clip with consistent character details and native audio direction.

use_cases.title: Create vertical social clips
use_cases.description: Use the vertical aspect ratio example and prompt patterns for platform-ready short videos.

use_cases.title: Test AI video prompts
use_cases.description: Run lower cost 720p test generations before committing to longer or higher resolution outputs.

prompt_templates.title: Basic video generation
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a default clip
prompt_templates.prompt: Use HappyHorse 1.0 to generate a 5 second 1080p video of a calm sunrise over a mountain lake with gentle wind audio.

prompt_templates.title: Vertical short with settings
prompt_templates.scenario: Specify aspect ratio, duration, and watermark preference
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a 9:16 HappyHorse video for a social post. Duration 8 seconds, no watermark, prompt about a barista preparing espresso in warm morning light.

prompt_templates.title: Multi-shot character continuity
prompt_templates.scenario: Keep a character consistent across two beats
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate a HappyHorse 1.0 clip with two shots. Keep the same woman in a navy trench coat and blue scarf across both shots, first entering an alley and then stopping under an awning.

prompt_templates.title: Cost-aware iteration plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for staged prompt refinement
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me test this HappyHorse concept. First prepare a 720p 3 second trial command, then prepare a final 1080p 12 second command using the same seed if the test looks good.

output_examples.input: Generate a default HappyHorse video about an astronaut skiing on the moon.
output_examples.output: The assistant prepares a RunComfy text-to-video request with a cinematic motion prompt, default 16:9 aspect ratio, 1080p resolution, and a local output directory.

output_examples.input: Make this idea work for a vertical product ad.
output: Rewrites the prompt with one clear motion beat.
Uses 9:16 aspect ratio and a short duration.
Adds audio direction and warns about unsupported aspect ratios.

output_examples.input: Why did my command fail with exit code 65?
output_examples.output: The assistant explains that exit code 65 means bad input JSON or schema mismatch, then checks duration, resolution, and aspect ratio values.

best_practices: Start with a short 720p test before generating longer 1080p clips.
Describe motion over time and include one clear visual beat per clip.
Store RunComfy credentials securely and avoid sharing prompts that contain sensitive information.
anti_patterns: Do not use unsupported aspect ratios or durations outside the documented range.
Do not combine many unrelated actions in one short clip prompt.
Do not assume generated third-party output URLs are safe outside the documented RunComfy domains.

faq.question: Does this skill run video generation locally?
faq.answer: No. It uses the local RunComfy CLI to submit jobs to the RunComfy Model API.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it support image-to-video?
faq.answer: This skill documents the text-to-video endpoint. Image-to-video requires a separate pipeline.

faq.question: What credentials are required?
faq.answer: A RunComfy account is required. Users can sign in with the CLI or set RUNCOMFY_TOKEN in CI.

faq.question: Can it generate clips longer than 15 seconds?
faq.answer: No. The documented endpoint caps duration at 15 seconds, so longer stories should be split into clips.

faq.question: What data leaves my machine?
faq.answer: Prompts and generation settings are sent to RunComfy, and generated output files are downloaded from RunComfy domains.
